newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shippers urge action on air surcharges.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shippers urge action on air surcharges.

text.p: OTM, the traffic managers organisation in Belgium, has urged its members not to use carriers that are introducing fuel surcharges.
Secretary of OTM, Fred Nuhaan, said the shippers group had called on its members to ban the use of carriers implementing the fuel surcharges.
"We have suggested that they avoid carriers adding these charges as much as possible and instead they should use the integrators," said Nuhaan.

OTM is encouraging the use of the express operators and Belgium's national carrier, Sabena, because the airline is not introducing surcharges until December 1. "After that we will try and use other airlines," he said.
Belgium's shippers are objecting to the move by the airlines on four counts.
Nuhaan said the airlines applied the surcharges at very short notice. "We have requested that the airlines postpone the introduction until at least December."
OTM members feel that the surcharge is also unfair in that with some carriers the same amount is applied if cargo is being shipped intra- Europe or to Australia, he said.
Several carriers are charging half the surcharge for intra-European traffic. BA's European rate is BF 1.5 and for other destinations BF 3.

A third point of contention concerns the system of documentary credits which are used if the goods are being shipped to an unknown consignee. This enables the shipper to get paid once they prove they have shipped the goods.

Because this surcharge is added into a separate box on the air way bill it is "uncollectable", he said. Many countries will not recognise it, he added. "The airlines just have not given this enough thought."

OTM is also calling for specific information regarding the withdrawal of the surcharges. "Only a few airlines have been specific in stating that the surcharges will be withdrawn once fuel prices reach their July levels," he added.

"There has been a totally unprofessional approach to this. But what can we do? We have to ship products to our customers," Nuhaan stated, adding that OTM had considered court action but decided against it.
"We just hope we will be able to meet with the airlines in the very near future and until then we will avoid these carriers as much as possible."
